exposure: Doppler study findings (e.g., uterine artery PI, diastolic notch, umbilical artery Doppler, MCA PI Doppler)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 100 primigravida patients aged 18 to 35 years, attending antenatal outpatient department and screened between 18 to 22 weeks of gestation.
finding: Elevated uterine artery pulsatility index (PI) and diastolic notch were superior in predicting Preeclampsia, while specific Doppler findings (umbilical artery or MCA PI) varied in their predictive utility for perinatal outcome depending on gestational age.
mod_finding: Patients with abnormal Doppler findings had a significantly higher rate of LSCS (70.83%) compared to those with normal Doppler findings (10.53%).
followup_time: Up to 14 days post-delivery (for NICU stay)
birth_weight: Ranged from 1.40 kg to 3.24 kg, with a mean of 2.7023 kg.
gest_age: Initial screening at 18-22 weeks, follow-up after 30 weeks, and mean gestational age at delivery was 37.68 weeks.
